gap: No result ChatGPT got states that tool changing can be added to a Prusa printer someone already owns only with the kit made for that model: the INDX kit for CORE One/+ is $693.52 for 4 tools, the separate kit for CORE One L/L+ is $763.80, the CORE One+ kit does not fit the L, and both ship after February 2027; also, an original XL with a Dwarf board marked 07 or lower needs new Dwarf boards before the $230.56 XL+ upgrade.
standout_why: I compared against 3dtoolchangers.com/printers (cited) and 3dprinteray.com/toolchanger-printers (cited). I also read 3dtoolchangers.com/compare/prusa-core-one-plus-indx-vs-snapmaker-u1 (top result). The 3dtoolchangers pages say nothing about conversion kits, XL upgrades, Dwarf boards or which enclosure fits which printer. 3dprinteray treats INDX as one kit that 'fits the Prusa CORE One, CORE One+ and CORE One L+'. Prusa's own pages say there is a separate kit for CORE One L/L+ and that the CORE One+ kit does not fit the L. 3dprinteray also lacks the parts that differ between the Gen 1 and Gen 2 kits, the kit prices and the February 2027 ship date. Neither rival mentions the Dwarf board 08+ rule for the XL to XL+ upgrade or that the new enclosure fits the XL+ only. I could not read the body of the cited Tom's Hardware page, so it is not ruled out.
decides: This does not change the pick for a buyer with no printer. ChatGPT's list stands: Snapmaker U1 is the cheapest true toolhead changer, and the XL+ is the large-format choice. It does change the answer for anyone who already owns a Prusa. A CORE One/+ owner can get INDX for $693.52 instead of $1,999 for an assembled printer, but delivery is after February 2027. A CORE One L owner must buy the L kit. An original XL owner should get the $230.56 XL+ upgrade, after checking the Dwarf board number, rather than buy a new XL+ at $3,899 or more. The original XL can't use the new 50 °C enclosure, so anyone buying a used original XL is stuck with the older enclosure until they upgrade.

findings.product: Prusa INDX 4-Tool Conversion Kit for CORE One/+
findings.label: Price, fit and ship date
findings.value: $693.52 (4-tool kit, US shipping selected); listed as compatible with 'CORE One/+'; build volume after conversion 248 × 205 × 270 mm (2 mm less in X, 15 mm less in Y); 'New orders are estimated to ship after February 2027'
findings.source_title: INDX 4-Tool Conversion Kit for CORE One+ (Gen2) | Original Prusa 3D printers directly from Josef Prusa
findings.note: Opened both on 2026-11-10: this URL and /product/indx-4-tool-conversion-kit-for-core-one/, which shows the same title, price, fit and ship date. The page's long 'not compatible with' list also names 'CORE One+ (Gen 2)', which contradicts the title. Treat the title and the compatible field as authoritative and flag the conflict. The odd $693.52 figure suggests a currency conversion.

findings.product: Prusa INDX Conversion Kit for CORE One/+
findings.label: Parts that differ between Gen 1 and Gen 2
findings.value: Original CORE One+: GT 1.5 belts and thermal expansion joints included. CORE One+ (Gen 2): both 'Not included - already present on the printer'
findings.source_title: INDX 4-Tool Conversion Kit for CORE One+ (Gen2) | Prusa
findings.note: The maker's page shows contents per printer generation. MatterHackers' CORE One/+ listing (https://www.matterhackers.com/store/l/prusa-indx-multi-tool-conversion-kit-for-core-one/sk/MRAR16SU, read 2026-11-10) says a standard CORE One becomes a CORE One+ once INDX is installed, the kit is 'not compatible with MK4S, MK3S+, or other 3D printers', and 'The CORE One+ version is not compatible with the L.'

findings.product: Prusa INDX 4-Tool Conversion Kit for CORE One L
findings.label: Separate kit for the L
findings.value: $763.80; 'Made for Prusa CORE One L and L+'; build volume after conversion 298 × 275 × 330 mm; 4-tool kit can be expanded to 8 tools later; ships after February 2027; install takes about 5–6 hours (user reports quoted by Prusa)
findings.source_title: INDX 4-Tool Conversion Kit for CORE One L | Prusa
findings.note: Prusa's 'not compatible' list on this page includes CORE One+ (Gen 2). The page says the final price is calculated at checkout.

findings.label: Assembled vs kit prices and nozzle sizes
findings.value: 4 tools: $1,999 assembled / $1,699 kit. 8 tools: $2,249 assembled / $1,949 kit. Supported nozzles: 0.25, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0 mm. Max nozzle temperature 300 °C. 1.75 mm filament, any brand.
findings.source_title: Prusa CORE One+ (Gen 2) INDX | Multi-Material Toolchanger 3D Printer
findings.note: The page's FAQ 'Which printers does INDX support?' had no answer in the text I could read.

findings.label: Limits Prusa states
findings.value: Nozzles are 'surface-hardened rather than fully hardened'. Prusa's wear guidance per nozzle: roughly 10 kg of PETG-CF, 5 kg of PC-CF or 0.5 kg of highly abrasive filament. Prusa staff, replying in the comments: 'no current plans to add the INDX to the XL'.
findings.source_title: Prusa CORE One+ (Gen 2) INDX, Shipping Has Started, Complete Printers Open for Orders
findings.note: The wear figures are from the article itself. The XL statement is a comment by Tommy_Prusa3D (community manager), not the article body. The article says there are separate kit versions for CORE One+ and CORE One+ (Gen 2).

findings.product: Prusa XL to XL+ Upgrade (1 tool head, no nozzle)
findings.label: Upgrade price and board requirement
findings.value: $230.56. 'If your Dwarf board is marked with a number 07 or lower, it is necessary to replace it with a new one before upgrading'; boards marked 08 or higher are fine. Kit includes GT1.5 belts and pulleys, 30+ PC/PCCF printed parts and new print fans; the tool offset sensor comes only in the 2- and 5-tool versions.
findings.source_title: Prusa XL to Prusa XL+ Upgrade - 1 Tool Head (no Nozzle) | Prusa
findings.note: Lead time listed as 5–6 weeks. The page is unclear about nozzles: one line says a 'CHT 0,4 nozzle' is included, while the package list says 'CHT nozzles (optional)'.

findings.label: Enclosure and heater fit
findings.value: 'The new Enclosure is compatible with the XL+ only!' The heater add-on is listed as not compatible with the XL. The original XL enclosure can be kept after upgrading to XL+ but 'won't reach 50°C like the new one'.
findings.source_title: Prusa XL+ Single-Tool | Original Prusa 3D printers directly from Josef Prusa
findings.note: The 'won't reach 50°C' and 'keep it' wording is from the XL to XL+ upgrade page (https://www.prusa3d.com/product/prusa-xl-to-prusa-xl-upgrade/, read 2026-11-10). The XL+ page says 'Add toolheads any time - the frame is ready', shows $2,128.70 for the single-tool XL+, says 'High Demand - Leadtime 6–7 weeks', and ships from EU and US warehouses.

findings.label: Toolheads and accessory fit
findings.value: Four independent, preheated toolheads. The page does not say more can be added. Optional Top Cover for high-temperature engineering filaments. RFID reads only Snapmaker's official filaments. Slicer: Snapmaker Orca, built on Orca Slicer.
findings.note: The maker page gives no price, nozzle options or firmware name.

unsourced: Bambu Lab Vortek Upgrade Kit fit for H2D, H2S and H2D Pro, firmware prerequisite and US price: us.store.bambulab.com returned 402/404, bambulab.com/en-us/h2c returned 403, and searches did not surface the Bambu wiki page. Only resellers and forums had it, so I left it out.
Snapmaker U1 US price today and its compatible nozzle/hotend options (hardened steel, sizes): the US Shopify store returned HTTP 429 twice, and the maker page lists neither.
Whether Flashforge Creator 5 and Creator 5 Pro toolheads are interchangeable: not researched within the tool budget.
Body of the cited Tom's Hardware best-3D-printers page (2026-11-07): the fetch returned only the title, so I could not check it for compatibility statements.

Whether the CORE One/+ INDX kit fits an original non-plus CORE One without a separate upgrade: Prusa's page Q&A has no answer and resellers disagree. MatterHackers says installing INDX makes a CORE One a CORE One+.
